QFE of 1,017 hPa

questions.text: What does relative humidity compare at a specified air temperature?
options: The actual water-vapour content with the saturation water-vapour content at that temperature
The mass of water vapour with the total mass of moist air
The mass of water vapour with the mass of dry air
The mass of water vapour with the volume of the air parcel

questions.text: On a clear, moist night with light wind over land, which cooling process produces radiation fog near the surface?
options: The ground loses heat by radiation and cools the air touching it to its dewpoint
Warm moist air is transported horizontally over a colder surface
Air is forced up a slope and cools by expansion until saturated
Water evaporates into colder air flowing across a warmer water surface

questions.text: For approximately steady, large-scale surface flow in the Northern Hemisphere away from strong terrain effects, how does air circulate around a high and a low?
options: Clockwise and outward around the high; anticlockwise and inward around the low
Clockwise and inward around the high; anticlockwise and outward around the low
Anticlockwise and outward around the high; clockwise and inward around the low
Anticlockwise and inward around the high; clockwise and outward around the low

questions.text: A pilot descends from above the friction layer toward flat land in the Northern Hemisphere. The pressure pattern is steady, with no front or local breeze. What change in mean wind is normally expected as surface friction increases?
options: It backs and slows
It veers and slows
It backs and speeds up
It veers and speeds up

questions.text: Over flat inland terrain in the Northern Hemisphere, the pressure pattern stays steady and local breezes are absent. Daytime heating strengthens turbulent mixing with air above the friction layer. What normally happens to the surface mean wind?
options: It veers and speeds up
It backs and speeds up
It veers and slows
It backs and slows

questions.text: Which feature is a weather front?
options: A relatively narrow transition zone separating air masses with different temperature or moisture characteristics
A line connecting places with equal sea-level pressure
An elongated zone of relatively low pressure that need not separate different air masses
A level where a rising air parcel first becomes saturated

270° magnetic/24 kt

270° true/30 kt

questions.text: At one level and time, forecast point A gives 350° true/10 kt and +4°C; point B gives 010° true/20 kt and −4°C. For this planning exercise, interpolate direction along the shortest arc through north and speed and temperature linearly. What is the estimate halfway between A and B?

questions.text: Moist stable air is forced across a mountain range and produces a classic foehn on the lee side. What weather is most likely on the windward side where the moist air is rising?
options: Orographic cloud, possible precipitation and obscured mountains
Only warm, dry descending air with no possibility of cloud
The same dry-air warming as on the lee side, because both slopes have descending flow
No change in air temperature or saturation as the air rises

questions.text: Which regional wind is channelled through the Rhône valley toward the Mediterranean, often cold, dry and gusty?
options: Mistral
Bora
Foehn
Sea breeze

questions.text: Which regional wind is associated with very cold air spilling across mountain barriers toward the northern Adriatic coast, producing strong gusts and downslope turbulence?
options: Bora
A warm foehn by definition
A daytime sea breeze
Anabatic upslope flow

questions.text: Beyond temporary visual disturbance or radio interference, what direct physical damage can an aircraft lightning strike cause?
options: Local skin punctures or damage at exposed entry/exit points
Only temporary radio noise, because an airborne aircraft cannot carry a lightning current
Only a magnetic-compass deviation, with the skin guaranteed to remain intact
No physical damage if static discharge wicks are installed

questions.text: What creates a thunderstorm gust front near the surface?
options: The leading boundary of cool downdraught air spreading outward after reaching the ground
The warm air rising into the cloud before any downdraught has formed
The freezing level moving downward inside a stationary cloud
Only the electrical discharge from a lightning strike with no air movement

questions.text: Strong wind aloft crosses a mountain ridge perpendicular to it, while an aerodrome lies in a sheltered lee valley. What should a pilot anticipate when descending into the valley?
options: Abrupt changes in wind direction/speed, rotors and possible downdraughts; the sheltered surface wind does not describe the entire approach
Only a smooth decrease in wind speed with no possible directional change
Exactly the same wind at all heights because the aerodrome is sheltered
A guaranteed tailwind-free approach whenever surface wind is calm

questions.text: Which weather product primarily displays mean-sea-level pressure isobars, pressure centres and surface fronts?
options: Surface analysis chart
A precipitation-radar reflectivity image
A spot wind-and-temperature-aloft table
An aerodrome runway visual range report

questions.text: For a broad overview of cloud cover and a separate view of precipitation echoes, which products are normally paired in weather briefing?
options: Satellite imagery for cloud patterns and weather radar for precipitation echoes
Weather radar for all thin non-precipitating cirrus and satellite imagery only for surface pressure
An ATIS report for global cloud images and a barograph for precipitation location
A pressure-only chart for cloud photographs and a METAR for radar echoes

questions.text: Which information can an ATIS broadcast normally add to the meteorological observation contained in a METAR?
options: Operational details such as runway in use and transition level
A guarantee that an approach clearance has been issued to every listening aircraft
The aircraft’s individual fuel endurance calculated by ATC
A replacement for all route SIGMETs and the aircraft flight manual

questions.text: In the ICAO scheme, a SIGMET identifies significant en-route weather within which type of named airspace area?

Only a single aerodrome’s traffic circuit
Only the runway strip within an aerodrome
Only one operator’s aircraft cabin

questions.text: With comparable pressure gradients and height above the surface, over which terrain is surface friction generally strongest?
options: Rough terrain with trees and buildings
A smooth open-water surface
Flat ice with few obstacles

questions.text: What is the broad atmospheric boundary separating colder polar air from warmer subtropical air in the mid-latitudes called?
options: Polar front

Intertropical convergence zone
Subtropical high-pressure belt

questions.text: On a sunny day, a mountain slope heats the air touching it. The resulting local flow moves uphill. What is this wind called?
options: Anabatic wind

questions.text: For the same mass of water near 0°C, which of these changes releases more latent heat to its surroundings?

Freezing from liquid to ice, rather than condensation from vapour to liquid
Melting ice, because melting releases rather than absorbs latent heat
Evaporating liquid, because evaporation releases rather than absorbs latent heat

options: Conditionally unstable: unsaturated lifting is initially stable, but saturated lifting can become unstable
Absolutely stable for both saturated and unsaturated parcels
Absolutely unstable even before a parcel reaches saturation

questions.text: A high cloud consists of thin, detached white filaments with a fibrous, hair-like appearance. Which cloud genus best fits this description?
options: Cirrus
Stratus
Cumulus
Nimbostratus

8000 m at all latitudes
16000 m at all latitudes
50000 m, approximately 164000 ft

questions.text: Moist, stable air is carried uphill by a sustained wind and cools by expansion until saturated close to the slope. Which fog formation mechanism is this?
options: Upslope(orographic)fog
Radiation fog caused by nocturnal ground cooling
Steam fog caused by evaporation from warm water into cold air
Advection fog caused solely by cooling over a flat colder surface

questions.text: Before substantial modification along its track, how is a cold, dry air mass formed over a high-latitude continental interior classified?
options: Continental polar(cP)
Maritime polar(mP)
Continental tropical(cT)
Maritime tropical(mT)

options: Cold front

questions.text: Which surface front uses the semicircle-marked standard line shown in this drawing?
options: Warm front
Cold front
Occluded front
Stationary front

questions.text: A typical fast-moving cold front has passed and the area is now in colder, unstable air with no persistent low cloud layer. Which weather pattern is most likely behind the frontal band?
options: Improved visibility between cumulus clouds and scattered showers, with cooler air and rising pressure
A steadily lowering widespread nimbostratus layer ahead of a warm front
Warmer, increasingly humid air with continuously falling pressure
Permanent CAVOK with no possible turbulence or showers

questions.text: Two contrasting air masses meet, but their boundary has little or no horizontal movement. What type of front is this?
options: Stationary front
Cold front advancing into warm air
Warm front advancing into cold air

questions.text: In a typical passing wave depression, a station first meets the warm front, then the warm sector, then the cold front. Which simplified pressure sequence is normally expected?
options: Falling ahead of the warm front, relatively steady in the warm sector, rising after the cold front
Rising ahead of the warm front, rising rapidly in the warm sector, falling after the cold front
Constant throughout because pressure changes only with aircraft altitude
Falling after the cold front while temperature and dewpoint must rise

questions.text: In the idealised global circulation, near which latitudes are the subtropical belts of persistent high pressure centred?
options: About 30°north and 30°south
At the Equator only
About 60°north and 60°south
Exactly at both magnetic poles

questions.text: In the idealised mid-latitude circulation, what is the predominant large-scale wind component that generally carries many weather systems across temperate regions?
options: Westerly flow, broadly from west toward east
Easterly flow from east toward west at every level and time
No prevailing flow because Coriolis force is zero at 45°latitude
Flow permanently from the Equator straight toward each pole with no east-west component

questions.text: When the synoptic pressure gradient is weak on a sunny day, why can a local sea breeze or upslope breeze dominate the surface wind?
options: Small-scale heating differences can drive a circulation while the background synoptic wind is weak
Local heating differences stop whenever isobars are widely spaced
Coriolis force alone creates every sea breeze even with no temperature difference

questions.text: A persistent winter anticyclone traps moist air beneath an inversion, with light wind and weak daytime heating. Which VFR-weather hazard can persist despite high surface pressure?

Unlimited visibility and cloud-free skies are guaranteed by the high pressure alone
Every trapped low cloud must immediately become a cumulonimbus

questions.text: On a clear, moist night, where can cold-air drainage make radiation or valley fog develop first compared with nearby hilltops?
options: At low points and valley floors where cool, dense air accumulates
Only at the highest exposed peak
Only over warm water as steam fog
At all heights simultaneously regardless of terrain

questions.text: Which description best fits the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)?

A permanent belt of descending dry air at 30° latitude in both hemispheres

Continual veering identical to a station south of the low
No directional change around any moving low

Steam fog from cold air passing over warm water
Radiation fog solely from nocturnal ground cooling
Upslope fog solely from terrain lifting

Toward lower pressure

questions.text: In a standard surface weather station plot, what does the shading of the central station circle represent?
options: Amount of sky covered by cloud
Cloud-base height above MSL
Sea-level pressure in hPa
Wind speed in knots

To seal the sensor in stagnant air so outside changes cannot reach it
To make the sensor measure the temperature of the ground instead of air

Unburnt fuel remains as a permanent liquid trail
Dry soot alone forms the visible trail, without condensed water or ice

Continue on track and wait for the ice to remove itself

Cold, dense air accumulating in a valley at night

Mass per unit volume
Force multiplied by area

options: Northeasterly in the Northern Hemisphere and southeasterly in the Southern Hemisphere
Southeasterly in the Northern Hemisphere and northeasterly in the Southern Hemisphere
Westerly in both hemispheres, away from the Equator
Northerly in both hemispheres, away from the subtropical highs

A wind that reverses every few minutes solely because of gusts
A permanent wind from exactly the same direction in every season

It is always limited to a harmless brittle film that breaks away by itself

Exactly at solar noon
Always immediately after sunset
Only in the middle of the afternoon

Advection fog caused by warm moist air cooling over a colder surface
Radiation fog formed solely by nighttime ground cooling

questions.text: What is a pre-frontal squall line?

The clear, subsiding centre of an anticyclone

A small rising thermal that never produces downdraughts

The elevation of the ground itself

In the very centre of the clear eye
Only at a fixed 500 km radius from the centre

A sea breeze

questions.text: What approximate cloud-base range defines the low-cloud level in temperate regions?

About 6500–23000 ft
Always above the tropopause

questions.text: How does hail grow within a thunderstorm?
options: Ice particles collect supercooled liquid drops that freeze onto them while strong updraughts support them
It forms solely when ordinary rain freezes after leaving the cloud
It grows only by absorbing water vapour with no liquid-water collisions
It is produced by frost deposited on the ground and lifted into the cloud

questions.text: Before beginning an approach in a light aircraft, the pilot receives a warning of severe low-level wind shear on final. A safe delay or diversion is available. What is the prudent planning response?
options: Delay the approach or divert rather than deliberately enter the reported severe shear
Ignore the warning if the surface wind is below the aircraft crosswind limit
Continue normally because ATC will cancel the warning before any danger occurs
Simply add a fixed 20 kt to approach speed for every aircraft type

questions.text: In UK altimetry terminology, what does a Regional Pressure Setting(RPS), historically called regional QNH, represent?
options: The lowest forecast mean-sea-level pressure within the specified altimeter-setting region
The average of all observed QFEs at aerodromes within that region
The highest observed QNH in the region
The universal 1013.25 hPa standard pressure setting

questions.text: A fictional METAR observed at 1630 UTC includes the TREND BECMG AT1800 9999 NSW. What does AT1800 specify?
options: The change is expected at 1800 UTC within the TREND period
The METAR observation was made at 1800 UTC
The TAF is valid for 18 hours
The change must last for exactly 1800 minutes

questions.text: An aerodrome is 600 m AMSL. The base of fair-weather cumulus is 1830 m AMSL and surface temperature is 22°C. Using cloud-base height above the aerodrome≈123×(temperature−dewpoint) metres, estimate the surface dewpoint.
Use this fictional TAF: TAF LTAC 121000 Z 1212/1221 18008 KT 6000 -RA BKN012 FM121600 26012 KT 9999 SCT030 =. What prevailing conditions are forecast at 1630 UTC on the 12 th?
options: 260° true/12 kt, 10 km or more visibility, scattered cloud at 3000 ft and no significant weather specified
180° true/8 kt with light rain until 2100 UTC, because FM changes cloud only
The new conditions apply only for a brief TEMPO fluctuation then revert to the initial forecast
The new conditions begin at 1216 UTC rather than 1600 UTC

questions.text: A pilot needs forecast areas of significant icing/turbulence and also the wind and temperature at a planned altitude. Which pair of products serves these two purposes respectively?
options: A significant-weather chart(SWC/SIGWX), and a wind-and-temperature-aloft forecast
A wind-and-temperature-aloft forecast, and a significant-weather chart(SWC/SIGWX)
An aerodrome METAR, and an aerodrome TAF
A surface-pressure analysis chart, and a visible satellite image

questions.text: In an aerodrome weather report, which abbreviation indicates that the stated phenomenon is in the vicinity rather than at the aerodrome itself?
options: VC
RE
BC
MI

questions.text: On a surface-pressure chart, what is the relatively neutral saddle region between two highs and two lows called?
options: A col
A ridge
A trough
The centre of a depression

questions.text: Which meteorological instrument is designed to measure the humidity of air?
options: Hygrometer
Barometer
Anemometer
Ceilometer

questions.text: In unsaturated air flowing over a correctly wetted thermometer wick, why is wet-bulb temperature lower than dry-bulb temperature?
options: Evaporation from the wick removes heat from the thermometer
Condensation on the wick releases heat into the thermometer
The wet wick measures the dewpoint directly, without evaporative cooling
The damp wick blocks heat transfer and reads a different colder air mass

questions.text: An unsaturated parcel near the ground cools on a clear night. Before condensation begins, assume pressure and water-vapour content remain constant. How do temperature, relative humidity and dewpoint change?
options: Temperature falls, relative humidity rises, dewpoint stays approximately constant
Temperature falls, relative humidity falls, dewpoint stays approximately constant
Temperature falls, relative humidity rises, dewpoint rises by the same amount
Temperature falls, relative humidity stays constant, dewpoint falls by the same amount

questions.text: An unsaturated air parcel is lifted a short distance and remains unsaturated. The environmental lapse rate is 0.7°C/100 m and the dry adiabatic lapse rate is 1.0°C/100 m. What tendency does the displaced parcel have?
options: It becomes colder than its surroundings and tends to sink back
It becomes warmer than its surroundings and continues rising freely
It stays at the same temperature as its surroundings and is neutrally stable
Its stability cannot be assessed unless its starting relative humidity was 100%

questions.text: A strong, steady wind blows from west to east across a ridge. An aircraft approaches the ridge from the east in a mountain-wave situation. Which vertical-flow sequence is normally expected close to the ridge as it crosses to the west?
options: Downdraught on the eastern lee side, then updraught on the western windward side
Updraught on the eastern lee side, then downdraught on the western windward side
Updraughts on both sides because air rises over all elevated terrain
Downdraughts on both sides because the aircraft is flying into the wind

questions.text: In the usual life cycle of a single thunderstorm cell, which stage contains strong updraughts alongside precipitation-driven downdraughts?
options: Mature stage
Initial cumulus stage
Dissipating stage after the updraught has ended
Every stage has equally strong simultaneous updraughts and downdraughts

questions.text: Which instrument produces a continuous trace of atmospheric pressure changes?
options: Barograph
Thermograph
Anemograph
Hygrometer

questions.text: During the initial cumulus stage of an ordinary thunderstorm cell, before a precipitation-driven downdraught develops, which vertical airflow dominates?
options: Updraughts
Downdraughts
Equal updraughts and downdraughts
No vertical airflow until rain reaches the ground

questions.text: A thin low-level mist layer lies beneath clear air. With terrain and airspace clearance and VMC maintained, an aircraft climbs safely above the layer. Why may its forward visibility improve?
options: Its forward line of sight now passes mainly through the clearer air above the layer
The reported ground visibility must improve by exactly the same amount
Downward visibility through the mist to the ground must become unlimited
A layer can obscure objects on the ground but cannot restrict air-to-air visibility

questions.text: Radiation fog covers an inland aerodrome at dawn. Surface wind then increases and turbulent mixing strengthens. Which development is physically possible?
options: The fog can disperse or lift into low stratus, depending on moisture and mixing depth
The fog must always thicken because any wind adds water vapour
The fog immediately becomes advection fog solely because wind speed increased
Wind cannot affect radiation fog until sunlight warms the ground

questions.text: A typical Northern Hemisphere depression passes north of a station. Its cold front brings colder, drier air. Which group of changes is most likely during passage?
options: Temperature and dewpoint fall, and the wind usually veers
Temperature and dewpoint fall, and the wind usually backs
Temperature falls but dewpoint rises, and the wind usually veers
Temperature and dewpoint rise, and the wind usually veers

questions.text: Small supercooled droplets freeze almost immediately on an aircraft leading edge, trapping air and producing a rough, milky, opaque deposit. What type of ice is this?
options: Rime ice
Clear ice
Hoar frost deposited directly from vapour
Mixed ice by definition, even when only one ice type is present

questions.text: A typical Northern Hemisphere depression passes north of a station. As its warm front passes the station, which shift of the surface wind is normally expected?
options: It veers, for example from southeast toward southwest
It backs, for example from southeast toward northeast
It remains in exactly the same direction through the entire frontal passage
It alternates north and south solely because a warm front has no temperature contrast

questions.text: Why can a small, pure cloud droplet remain liquid at a temperature below 0°C?
options: Freezing is not automatic at 0°C; droplets can supercool until freezing is triggered or temperatures become very low
The droplets must still be warmer than0°C whenever the surrounding air is subzero
Every liquid cloud droplet remains unfrozen solely because it contains enough salt
High relative humidity prevents droplets from freezing at any temperature

questions.text: In a fictional TAF, what does BECMG 1822/1902 BKN018 mean?
options: Becoming between 2200 UTC on the 18 th and 0200 UTC on the 19 th, broken cloud at 1800 ft above the aerodrome
Becoming between 1822 UTC and 1902 UTC, scattered cloud at 1800 ft above MSL
A temporary broken layer at 180 ft above the aerodrome throughout the 18 th
A change beginning at 1902 UTC on the 18 th, with an 1800 m cloud base

questions.text: A fixed-time SIGWX forecast chart is issued at 0600 UTC and labelled VALID1200 UTC. Which time does its plotted weather represent?
options: The expected weather at 1200 UTC
The observed weather at 0600 UTC
An unchanged weather forecast for every time from 0600 to 1800 UTC

questions.text: Depending on the published service, on which radio bands can voice VOLMET weather broadcasts be provided to aircraft?
options: HF and/or VHF, as ground-to-air broadcasts
LF only, as aircraft-to-ground position reports
UHF only, as aircraft-to-air weather discussions
